doc.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Jazz today and the loss of Herschel Evans
summary: Today's players have chops but stand on earlier musicians' shoulders; she wishes she could hear Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: An opera singer could fill it up. Yeah, it’s interesting. What’s your take on jazz today and the future?

Gee I don’t know. I have people I always go and see — Ahmad Jamal, I’m crazy about him. I would like to hear some big bands occasionally. Gosh, Jimmy Heath came by the table yesterday at the Life thing and said that he has a big band playing at the Iridium Room. I thought he said it was just last night. And I was too tired, but I think it’s for the whole week. So and he’s wonderful. But I said something, and I suppose I shouldn’t have said it to a newspaper, and it’s not a very original line, but I said the people today they have wonderful chops, and they’re well schooled you know, and it’s like the four minute mile, they can do stuff better than the people before them, skillfully. But they’re standing on the shoulders of these people in my photograph. You know, Dizzy and Mingus and Lester and Coleman Hawkins. I mean they’ve taken off from that. They’re great, but I’d give anything if I could hear Herschel Evans again.
He died awful young, didn’t he?
Yeah. Too soon for me. I’m not sure, as I say, I’m not sure I ever, I must have heard him in person but don’t remember. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-
